newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Leader of banned Ivorian student group arrested.
newsitem.headline: Leader of banned Ivorian student group arrested.

text.p: Ivory Coast's security minister said on Tuesday that the head of a banned student group had been arrested for inciting student "disobedience" and would face prosecution.
"We have apprehended him and he will be placed at the disposition of the judicial authorities," the minister, Marcel Dibonan Kone, said on state television.

The television showed Guillaume Soro, the arrested secretary-general of the FESCI student federation, sitting alongside the minister, who described the student leader as the "main author of (student) disobedience".
Ivory Coast's universities have been regularly shaken by student unrest over the years.
An Ivorian court jailed three FESCI activists on January 7 for inciting violence and disrupting public order.

FESCI called a widely followed strike from January 22 to 24 to demand payment of grant arrears and protest against academic reforms and the mystery death of a student after security forces broke up a meeting at a university hall of residence.
A university lecturers' union staged a 48-hour strike last week to protest at the situation in Ivorian universities. It drew a mixed response.
FESCI has been a thorn in the side of the Ivorian authorities since its creation in 1990 as pressure built within the West African nation for multi-party democracy.
The authorities banned it in 1991 after the killing of a student, widely believed to be in the pay of the government. He was beaten to death. The government blamed FESCI.
